Definition: Sin — missing the mark; rebellion, guilt and the corrupted condition that separates humanity from God and fractures everything else.
BiblicalUsage: Hamartia names sin as both acts we commit and a power that enslaves. All have sinned and fall short of God's glory — yet John announces the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
TheologicalSignificance: Naming hamartia honestly is the first step to hope: if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive. The diagnosis is grave precisely because the cure is glorious.
